pr_body:
modules: mbedtls: Fix init hang issue
libc: common: Fix init hang issue

In device init phase, it will call _mbedtls_init before malloc_prepare
as mbedtls has higher priority defined in SYS_INIT..
_mbedtls_init() will call psa_crypto_init() and malloc buffer,
but z_malloc_heap is not initialized, which will cause device hang.
Should call malloc_prepare() before _mbedtls_init to fix this issue,
so exchange their priority to init in SYS_INIT.

Fixes #74980
pr_comments:
I had issues because of this with the ethos-u drivers that’s currently requiring a malloc call during device driver initialization, which happens before malloc_prepare is called.

What would be the reason for not doing this ASAP during boot? Or is it a matter where drivers relying on this should be given a lower priority and done at a later stage (if possible, I’m not familiar with this)?

> I had issues because of this with the ethos-u drivers that’s currently requiring a malloc call during device driver initialization, which happens before malloc_prepare is called.
> 
> What would be the reason for not doing this ASAP during boot? Or is it a matter where drivers relying on this should be given a lower priority and done at a later stage (if possible, I’m not familiar with this)?

Services initialization is "complicated" now. The priority I suggest is just an example, it can be `0` as in this PR. I would just make it through a symbol in case a target needs a different priority. Since we are talking about the C library I don't see a problem having a specific symbol for that.
Malloc is kind of horrible in drivers and critical subsystems. It would be great if it could be avoided entirely.
Hi @keith-packard , can you please review again?

>  Malloc is kind of horrible in drivers and critical subsystems. It would be great if it could be avoided entirely.

An alternative here would be to enforce that: assert or panic if you get a malloc call before libc initialization and force subsystems that want to do clumsy things to finesse things themselves...

> Malloc is kind of horrible in drivers and critical subsystems. It would be great if it could be avoided entirely.

While I tend to agree, this problem is really between mbedtls and libc initialization order. Not sure I characterize mbedtls as a driver... maybe a critical subsystem but it is a large one from third-party. 

But @andyross suggestion is a good one to generally consider to see if we can find other entities that are probably failing this priority inversion. Although this might cause a bunch of new, valid bugs to be added ;-).

Adding the following in the various alloc routines (malloc, aligned_alloc, realloc?, free?) should capture this problem. The z_malloc_heap is defined as a static but should be in the bss section but if we want to ensure that we could define it with an assignments to set to NULL:

`
	__ASSERT(z_malloc_heap.heap != NULL, "Priority inversion, malloc_prepare() has not been called");
`

I can update my coworker's PR with this to help facilitate things if this is deemed a good idea or we can submit a separate PR to do this.

issue_context.title: mbedtls and libc initialization priority problem leads to device hanging
issue_context.body:
In device init phase, it will call _mbedtls_init before malloc_prepare as mbedtls has higher priority defined in SYS_INIT..
_mbedtls_init() will call psa_crypto_init() and malloc buffer, but z_malloc_heap is not initialized, which will cause device hang.
Should call malloc_prepare() before _mbedtls_init to fix this issue, so exchange their priority to init in SYS_INIT.

review_comments: There are dozens of other SYS_INIT call sites using priority level 0. Do you want to fix them all? Should we make this an error so that we can catch it in the future?
Fixing them all needs fully test, but now I only can find the issue between mbedtls and malloc on our device, so for the safety consideration, I will only change this one.
